h1: Senfeng fiber lasers — compact 4 × 4 ft machines to 80 kW plate gantries, the value line
intro: Senfeng is the value line of NovoTech's laser section, sold under its own brand: a very large manufacturer in Jinan, China — about 15,000 machines a year — that builds its own fiber sources and cutting heads, CE / FDA / ETL certified, at a price that puts a 12 kW laser within reach of a small shop. The range starts where few others do: single-table compact machines from 4 × 4 ft that ship in one container and cut the day they arrive; the NP open-type laser, six of which fit in a 40 ft container, the lowest-priced 12 kW machine in the catalogue; the enclosed H series with a 20-second pallet changer from 1.5 to 80 kW on tables to 8.3 × 40 ft; the HM that cuts sheet and Ø8.6″ tube on one machine; the R and TX plate gantries to 10 × 164 ft with ±45° bevel heads for shipyards and structural steel; five-axis and robot 3D lasers for formed parts; and coil-fed lines that cut straight from the coil. Loading towers, sheet storage and air-cutting packages for every model. Installed, trained and supported from Mississauga, ON, with a CSA-approved panel and NovoTech's warranty.

groups.title: Senfeng fiber lasers — the value line
groups.lead: From the first 4 × 4 ft machine to 60 kW plate gantries: compact, NP open-type, H series with pallet changer, sheet + tube, plate, 3D and coil-fed.

faq.q: Which Senfeng laser for a first machine?
faq.a: For most shops the SF1530 series or the SF3015NP: a 5 × 10 ft single table with 3 or 6 kW. The SF1530NP is fully enclosed with a lifting door and a pull-out table — the tidy choice for a shop that cuts a few hours a day; the SF3015NP is the open-type with loading from three sides and the lowest price per kilowatt. Choose 6 kW if you cut 1/4″ to 1/2″ regularly; 3 kW is enough for sheet to 3/16″. Step up to the H series when you need the pallet changer to keep the laser cutting while you load.

The NP is a single-table open machine: the operator loads between sheets, which is fine for a few sheets an hour. The H series is enclosed and has a pallet changer that swaps tables in 20 seconds, so loading overlaps cutting — a production machine for two shifts, with 1.5 to 80 kW and tables to 8.3 × 40 ft, and the one that takes the loading tower and sheet storage. HC is the compact build, H4 the fourth-generation machine with 2 G and 656 ft/min, H5 the heavy-load frame for 40 – 80 kW and 2″ plate.

faq.q: Own-brand sources and heads — what does that mean for support?
faq.a: Senfeng builds its own fiber sources, cutting heads and control cabinets, so parts come from one maker rather than three, and IPG, Raycus or Max sources can be specified instead. Senfeng Laser USA holds parts and has a service team; NovoTech installs, trains and services in Canada from Mississauga, with remote diagnostics through the control and a CSA-approved panel on every machine.

faq.q: What is the HM sheet-and-tube combination?
faq.a: An enclosed H series sheet laser with a rotary chuck and tube supports on the side: the same 6 to 30 kW source and head cut 5 × 10 to 8.3 × 20 ft sheet with the pallet changer and round, square or rectangular tube from Ø0.7 to 8.6″ and 20 ft long. For a shop that cuts both but cannot justify two machines — switching takes the time to load the tube.

The R and TX series are gantry lasers with 10 and 13 ft wide tables from 20 to 164 ft long and 6 to 60 kW sources, replacing plasma and flame cutting of plate to 2″ and beyond. The TX carries a ±45° bevel head so weld preparations are cut in the same pass; the TXP adds an oxy-fuel torch for plate to 4″ on the same table. Shipyards, structural steel, bridges and heavy equipment are the customers.

faq.q: When does a coil-fed line pay off?
faq.a: When the same thin material runs all day: enclosures, HVAC, appliance and automotive parts. The decoiler, leveller and laser work on one control, there is no sheet handling, no offcuts and no limit on part length. The SF15015C runs thin coil through an open-type laser; the SF1503CH takes coil to 1/8″ and 16.5 tons; the SF2012CH levels and cuts 5/16″ to 9/16″ plate from 22-ton coils with 12 to 80 kW.

faq.q: How does Senfeng compare with the Dener premium line?
faq.a: Dener is the premium line: Turkish-built with Precitec heads, IPG / nLIGHT sources, a heavier frame rated for 1.5 G and Dener Canada parts in Mississauga — the longer life at high duty. Senfeng costs less and covers sizes and powers Dener does not: 4 × 4 ft compact machines, 60 kW plate gantries, sheet-and-tube combos, 3D and coil-fed lasers. The comparison, the laser power guide and the capacity table for both lines are on the sheet laser cutters overview.

faq.q: What voltage do these machines run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models with a small enough motor. Manual machines have no electrics.
